column2: 中古英语 somet（头、顶）← 盎格鲁诺曼语 sumet／中古法语 sommet ← 古法语 som（最高处）＋ 指小后缀 -et ← 拉丁语 summum（最高处）
column3: the highest point of a mountain, or a meeting between heads of state
column5: They reached the summit just after dawn.|Leaders met at a summit in Geneva.
column6: the highest point, where nothing stands above – 再往上就没有了的那一点
column7: 顶峰：山的最高处|峰会：与会者是各国最高层，故借这个「最高」

column2: 中古英语 somoundre ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 somoundre ← 古法语 sumundre ← 拉丁语 summonēre（提醒、传唤），由 sub（在下）＋ monēre（提醒）构成
column3: to order someone officially to come or appear
column5: He was summoned to appear in court.|She summoned the courage to speak up.
column6: an order that brings someone to you – 一声令下，把人叫到跟前
column7: 传唤：官方要人到场，多用于法庭|召来：把人叫到自己这里|唤起：把「叫出来」用在勇气或记忆上

column2: 中古英语 sonne ← 古英语 sunne ← 原始日耳曼语 *sunnǭ（太阳）← 原始印欧语 *sóh₂wl̥（太阳）
column3: the star that gives light and heat to the earth
column5: The sun rose behind the hills.|Sit out of the sun for a while.
column6: the one body whose light and heat reach everything here – 光与热照到这里一切事物的那个天体
column7: 太阳：那个天体本身|日光：它照下来的那份光与热

column2: 中古英语 sonne-rys，即 sun ＋ rise；两支均出古英语（sunne 太阳、rīsan 升起）
column3: the time when the sun first appears in the morning
column5: We set off before sunrise.|The sky turns orange at sunrise.
column6: the moment the sun's edge clears the horizon – 日轮刚越过地平线那一刻
column7: 日出：太阳露出来这件事或这个时刻|黎明：天开始亮的那一段，稍宽于日出一瞬

column2: 中古英语 son-sett，即 sun ＋ set；1393 年前已见于 Gower 的《情人的忏悔》
column3: the time when the sun goes down in the evening
column5: The boat returned at sunset.|Clouds glowed red after sunset.
column6: the moment the sun's edge drops below the horizon – 日轮沉到地平线以下那一刻
column7: 日落：太阳落下这件事或这个时刻|黄昏：日落前后天色转暗的那一段

column2: 由 sun ＋ shine 复合而成；1250 年前后已见于中古英语 sunnesine
column3: the light and warmth that come directly from the sun
column5: The children played in the sunshine.|We had three days of sunshine.
column6: the sun's light falling on things and warming them – 日光落到东西上，同时带来暖意
column7: 阳光：直接照下来的那份光|晴好天气：整片天都放晴的那种日子

column2: 截自 super-（在上、超出）← 中古英语 super- ← 拉丁语 super（在上）；与 over、hyper 同源
column3: very good, or greater than usual
column5: That was a super idea.|He has super reflexes for his age.
column6: placed above the ordinary level – 高出一般水准之上
column7: 极好的：好到超出寻常|超级的：程度或规模比同类都大

column2: 美国英语 1933 年造词，由 super-（超出）＋ market（市场）构成；market 一支 ← 古法语 marchié ← 拉丁语 mercatus
column3: a large shop selling food and household goods, where customers serve themselves
column5: She buys her vegetables at the supermarket.|The supermarket opens at eight.
column6: a shop so large that customers fetch goods themselves – 铺面大到顾客自己取货
column7: 超市：日常简称|超级市场：全称，指这种自助的大型商店

column2: 由 super-（超出）＋ sonic（声音的）构成；sonic 一支 ← 拉丁语 sonus（声音）
column3: faster than the speed of sound
column5: The jet made a supersonic pass over the field.|Supersonic travel is very costly.
column6: moving faster than sound itself travels – 走得比声音本身还快

column2: 中古英语 soper ← 古法语 soper（进晚餐）← sope（汤），本义是喝汤那一餐
column3: a light evening meal, usually the last of the day
column5: We had soup and bread for supper.|She left a plate of supper on the stove.
column6: the last and lighter meal of the day – 一天里最后那顿，且吃得轻
column7: 晚餐：晚上那一餐|夜宵：更晚、更轻的那一顿

column2: 中古英语 surgen ← 古法语 surgir（升起、涌上）← 拉丁语 surgō（立起、涌起），由 sub（自下）＋ regō（伸直）构成
column3: a sudden powerful rush forward or upward
column5: A surge of water broke over the wall.|There was a surge in demand for masks.
column6: a mass rising and rushing all at once – 一股东西同时抬起来向前扑
column7: 激增：数量突然大幅抬升|涌动：水或人群成股地向前挤|猛涨：价格或水位一下抬高

column2: 中古英语 surgien ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 surgien ← 通俗拉丁语 *chirurgianus ← 拉丁语 chirurgus ← 希腊语 kheirourgos（动手做的人），由 kheir（手）＋ ergon（活儿）构成
column3: a doctor who treats illness or injury by cutting into the body
column5: The surgeon explained the risks beforehand.|She trained as a heart surgeon.
column6: a doctor whose treatment is done with the hands and a blade – 靠手与刀施治的医生

column2: 中古英语 surgerie ← 古法语 surgerie ← 拉丁语 chirurgia ← 希腊语 kheirourgia（手工操作），由 kheir（手）＋ ergon（活儿）构成
column3: medical treatment in which a doctor cuts into the body
column5: She needs surgery on her knee.|He works in the surgery department.
column6: treatment carried out by cutting into the body – 靠切开身体来施行的治疗
column7: 手术：具体的那一次切治|外科：以这种治法为主的医学分支

column2: 中古英语 surname，部分仿译古法语 surnum（附加之名）← 晚期拉丁语 supernomen，由 super-（在上、附加）＋ nomen（名）构成
column3: the family name shared by members of a household
column5: Please write your surname in capitals.|They share a surname but are not related.
column6: the part of a name that comes from the family, not the person – 名字里承自家族而非属于个人的那一半
column7: 姓氏：家族传下来的那部分名称|姓：同义的单字说法，多与「名」对举

column2: 中古英语 surrendren ← 古法语 surrendre，由 sur-（在上）＋ rendre（交还）构成；取代了古英语 on hand gān
column3: to stop fighting and give oneself up to the enemy
column5: The garrison surrendered at dawn.|He refused to surrender his passport.
column6: handing yourself or your hold over to the other side – 把自己或手里握着的交到对方手上
column7: 投降：停止抵抗，把自己交出去|放弃：把原本坚持的松开手|交出：把具体之物移交对方

column2: 中古英语 surveyen ← 古法语 surveer（俯看、监看），由 sur-（在上）＋ veoir（看）构成 ← 拉丁语 vidēre（看）
column3: a careful examination or measuring of something, or a set of questions put to many people
column5: The survey covered two thousand households.|Engineers made a survey of the site.
column6: looking over the whole of something from above – 从高处把整片看过一遍
column7: 调查：逐项问过、记下，得出整体情况|勘测：对地形逐点实测|概览：先整体看一遍，不究细节

column2: 由 survive ＋ -al 构成；survive 一支 ← 古法语 survivre ← 晚期拉丁语 supervivere（活得比…长）
column3: the state of continuing to live or exist, especially after danger
column5: Their survival depended on finding water.|The custom is a survival from medieval times.
column6: still being there after what should have ended it – 该结束的没结束，仍在那里
column7: 生存：维持活着这件事|存活：经过险境仍活下来|残存之物：旧时留到今天的遗存

column2: 盎格鲁诺曼语 survivre／古法语 survivre ← 晚期拉丁语 supervivere（活得更久），由 super（在上、超过）＋ vivere（活）构成
column3: to continue to live or exist after a difficult or dangerous event
column5: Only two passengers survived the crash.|The tree survived three hard winters.
column6: living on past the thing that could have ended you – 越过那件本可要命的事继续活着
column7: 存活：继续活下来|幸存：在灾祸中未死的那一部分|比…活得久：本义即「活得超过」，可接对象

column2: 中古英语 swolwen ← 古英语 swelgan（吞）← 原始日耳曼语 *swelganą（吞、大嚼）← 原始印欧语 *swelk-（咽下）
column3: to make food or drink go down the throat
column5: He swallowed the pill with water.|Swallows nest under the eaves each spring.
column6: sending something down the throat in one movement – 一动把东西送下喉咙
column7: 咽下：把口中之物送进食道|吞食：整个咽下，不加咀嚼|燕子：另一支同形异源的词，指那种尾开如叉的小鸟

column2: 英语 swamp 1624 年始见于北美记载，或借自荷兰语 zwamp（沼泽）；与中古低地德语 swamp（海绵、菌）同族，更早词源不明
column3: an area of low wet ground, often with trees or reeds
column5: Mosquitoes bred in the swamp behind the house.|We were swamped with applications.
column6: low ground so soaked that water stands on it – 低洼地泡得水停在上面
column7: 沼泽：积水不去、泥软的低地|湿地：同类地貌的通称|淹没：把「水漫上来」用到事务上，指多到应付不过来

column2: 中古英语 swan ← 古英语 swan ← 原始日耳曼语 *swanaz（天鹅，字面「会鸣的鸟」）← 原始印欧语 *swenh₂-（发声、歌唱）
column3: a large white water bird with a long neck
column5: A swan glided across the still water.|Swans nest by the far bank.
column6: a large white water bird whose neck curves long and high – 颈长而弯的大型白色水鸟

column2: 中古英语 swarm ← 古英语 swearm（群、众）← 原始日耳曼语 *swarmaz（群）← 原始印欧语 *swer-（嗡鸣）
column3: a large group of insects or people moving together
column5: A swarm of bees settled on the branch.|Tourists swarmed through the narrow lanes.
column6: many small things moving as one mass, with a hum – 许多小东西成团一起动，还带着嗡声
column7: 一群：数量多、聚成一团的那批|蜂群：特指蜜蜂聚成的那团|成群涌来：把这团东西的移动当动作说

column2: 英语 sway 出自早期 swey（倾倒、晃倒）← 中古英语 sweyen ← 古英语 *swǣġan（弯、倾）← 原始日耳曼语 *swaigijaną
column3: to move slowly from side to side
column5: The branches swayed in the wind.|His speech swayed several undecided voters.
column6: leaning to one side and back again without leaving the spot – 不离原处，只往两边来回倾
column7: 摇晃：整体左右来回倾|晃动：幅度小些的同一动作|左右影响：把「使之倾向一边」用到人的立场上

column2: 中古英语 sweren ← 古英语 swerian（起誓、就职宣誓）← 原始日耳曼语 *swarjaną（说、起誓）← 原始印欧语 *swer-（起誓）
column3: to make a solemn promise, or to use offensive language
column5: He swore to tell the whole truth.|She swore loudly when the glass broke.
column6: putting words out under a weight one is bound to – 把话说出来，同时把自己压在那句话上
column7: 发誓：郑重许下，自任其责|立誓：多用于就职或入会这类正式场合|骂脏话：同一个词的另一层，指出口不敬的话

column2: 中古英语 swete ← 古英语 swāt ← 原始日耳曼语 *swaitą ← 原始印欧语 *sweyd-（出汗）
column3: the salty liquid that comes out of the skin when hot or working hard
column5: Sweat ran down his back as he dug.|She wiped the sweat from her forehead.
column6: salty water the skin puts out to cool the body – 皮肤放出的咸水，为的是把身上的热带走
column7: 汗：那种液体本身|汗水：同义，偏重成滴流下的样子|出汗：把这件事当动作说

column2: 中古英语 swētere，即 sweat ＋ -er；sweat 一支 ← 古英语 swāt（汗）← 原始日耳曼语 *swaitą
column3: a warm knitted garment for the upper body
column5: He pulled a thick sweater over his head.|That sweater shrank in the wash.
column6: a knitted garment worn to keep the body warm – 织出来的一件，穿着为的是留住体温
column7: 毛衣：用毛线织的那种|针织衫：泛指这类以织法成形的上衣

column2: 中古英语 swepen ← 原始西日耳曼语 *swaipijan（挥、扫，古英语未见记载）← 原始日耳曼语 *swaipijaną
column3: to clean a floor by pushing dust along with a brush
column5: She swept the kitchen floor.|Searchlights swept across the water.
column6: pushing something along a surface in one long motion – 沿表面一路推过去，动作长而连贯
column7: 扫：用帚把碎屑推到一处|清除：把一片范围内的东西全推走|掠过：光或视线沿表面一路扫过

column2: 中古英语 swete ← 古英语 swēte ← 原始日耳曼语 *swōtuz（甜的）← 原始印欧语 *sweh₂dus（甜的）
column3: tasting of sugar, or pleasing to the senses
column5: The tea is too sweet for me.|She has a sweet voice.
column6: the taste sugar gives, and anything as pleasing as it – 糖给出的那种味道，以及一切同样悦人的
column7: 甜的：味觉上像糖的|悦人的：把这份好味挪到声音或气味上|温柔的：把它用到人的性情与举止上

column2: 中古英语 swellen ← 古英语 swellan（膨胀）← 原始日耳曼语 *swellaną（涨大），更早词源不明
column3: to become larger or rounder than before
column5: His ankle swelled after the fall.|The river swelled with melted snow.
column6: growing outward until it takes up more room – 向外长开，占的地方变多
column7: 膨胀：整体变大变鼓|肿起：身体某处因伤病而鼓起|上涨：水位或数量抬高，同是「变大」

column2: 中古英语 swift ← 古英语 swift（快的）← 原始日耳曼语 *swiftaz（快）← 原始印欧语 *(s)weyp-（旋、绕）
column3: moving or happening very quickly
column5: She gave a swift reply.|The bird made a swift turn over the water.
column6: covering the distance in very little time – 用极短的时间走完那段距离
column7: 迅速的：事情进行得快|敏捷的：动作快而利落
